Covers are served at full size today. The lexicon allows cover blobs up to 2,000,000 bytes, and the catalog replicas work (ADR 7) now captures and serves them as-is. Grids and feed strips on the planned iOS app would load the full blob where a thumbnail of roughly 30 KB would do, which matters on mobile data.

Proposal: a side worker that produces derived thumbnails (for example 600px and 200px WebP) for captured and proxied covers, cached by the original blob's CID, served by the existing cover proxy with an immutable cache lifetime.

Constraints:

- Never replace or re-encode the captured blob. A replica's proof depends on byte identity: the cover CID is in the signed record, and adopters re-upload identical bytes. Thumbnails are derived serving artifacts only.
- Erlang/OTP has no image codecs. The likely engine is `vix` (Elixir NIF binding to libvips, believed to ship precompiled NIFs with libvips bundled) behind a thin Gleam FFI module. That needs an Elixir/Mix toolchain at build time (Dockerfile change). Alternatives: `eimp` (needs libgd/libjpeg/libpng/libwebp in the image), `mogrify` (ImageMagick binary).
- A NIF crash takes the VM down. vix uses dirty schedulers, but consider running the worker as a separate release or sidecar so a bad image can't take ingest with it.

Trigger: build when the iOS grid shows the bandwidth or latency cost in practice, not before.

Questions to settle:

- Sizes and format (WebP vs AVIF) for grid, list row, and detail hero.
- In-process worker vs sidecar.
- Cache storage and eviction (disk volume vs object storage).

title.text: Serve resized cover thumbnails from a side worker

`cmd/kukicha-relay/promote.kuki` does not check a report's queue status before creating a tracker record, and `MarkPromoted` updates by id without requiring `status = 'queued'`.

This has two user-visible consequences:

1. Running `kukicha-relay --promote <id>` twice can create duplicate tracker records even when the row is already promoted.
2. If ticket creation succeeds but `MarkPromoted` fails, the command still exits successfully while the row remains queued. A natural operator retry creates another ticket.

The new Knot2 path in `relay-cob-tickets` preserves this pre-existing behavior. Its tests cover ordinary success, knot failure, and best-effort attestation failure, but not repeated promotion or a forced bookkeeping failure after a successful write.

Suggested follow-up:

- Reject promotion when the row is not queued, or make promotion stateful by storing the created ticket URI before retrying.
- Make `MarkPromoted` update only queued rows and surface the affected-row count.
- Add regression tests for both duplicate invocation and a successful write followed by failed bookkeeping.

Pre-change repro shape:

```text
queue a report
promote it once
promote the same id again
```

The second invocation files another tracker record rather than returning the existing one.

title.text: kukicha-relay: promote is not idempotent and can duplicate tickets after bookkeeping failure

body.text:
## Summary

`stdlib/sqlite.Open` can fail when two pools open the same database concurrently because the default pragma DSN is built from a Go map:

```text
sqlite3: invalid _pragma: sqlite3: database is locked
```

`openDefaults` contains both `journal_mode = WAL` and `busy_timeout = 5000`, but `openWithPragmas` iterates the map. Map iteration is unordered, so a connection can attempt the write-mode `journal_mode` pragma before installing its busy timeout. If another connection briefly holds the database lock, the first pragma fails instead of waiting.

## Reproducer

This was exposed reliably enough under the race suite by `cmd/kukicha-relay`’s concurrent schema migration test:

```text
go test -race ./cmd/kukicha-relay/ -run TestInitBugSchemaMigratesLegacyTables -count=...
```

Observed under `make test`:

```text
--- FAIL: TestInitBugSchemaMigratesLegacyTables (0.13s)
    main_test.go:762: concurrent migration: sqlite3: invalid _pragma: sqlite3: database is locked
```

The test opens two `OpenRelayQueue` pools concurrently against the same SQLite file. Either pool can lose the unordered-pragma race during `sqlite.Open`.

## Expected

A default `sqlite.Open` should install `busy_timeout` before any potentially locking write pragma, so concurrent first opens wait rather than fail.

## Actual

`openWithPragmas` emits pragmas in Go map order. `journal_mode=WAL` may run before `busy_timeout=5000`, producing an immediate lock failure.

## Proposed fix

Make DSN pragma emission deterministic and put `busy_timeout` first when present. Add a stdlib regression test that concurrently opens two default pools against one file and asserts both opens succeed.

## Notes

- The relay migration transaction is already serialized; this failure occurs earlier, during pool construction.
- The relay test exposed the bug because it deliberately exercises two simultaneous first opens after upgrade.

title.text: stdlib/sqlite: concurrent Open can run journal_mode before busy_timeout and fail with database is locked
